w: Built originally in France's Rhone River Valley, this small chapel was moved to a Long Island estate before a final journey to Marquette University's Milwaukee campus, where it was rededicated to Joan of Arc on 26 May 1966. Twice relocated across an ocean and a continent, it remains an active Catholic chapel.
s: A French chapel that crossed an ocean, then a continent
_facts: Originally built in the Rhone River Valley, France
Previously stood on Long Island, New York
Rededicated to Joan of Arc in Milwaukee on 26 May 1966
Located on the Marquette University campus, Archdiocese of Milwaukee

w: Milwaukee's first skyscraper, this 14-story neo-Gothic tower rose in 1891 and held the city's height record until City Hall topped it four years later. It came down in 1981, making it, at 235 feet, the second-tallest building ever demolished in Wisconsin; another tower now stands on its footprint.
_facts: Held the city height record until Milwaukee City Hall opened in 1895
Second-tallest building ever demolished in Wisconsin

w: Billed as Wisconsin's largest cold-storage house when it opened in 1892, this Romanesque Revival building in Walker's Point kept five stories chilled with river ice, switching to mechanical refrigeration after 1910. Its two-foot-thick, near-windowless walls held the cold for decades before a 2019 sale toward new use.
_facts: Built 1892, once billed as Wisconsin's largest cold-storage house
Two-foot-thick walls with few windows to retain cold
Originally cooled with river ice, switched to mechanical refrigeration after 1910
Sold to a developer in 2019 for conversion to new uses

w: Home to the Wisconsin State Fair since 1892, this West Allis fairground also holds the Milwaukee Mile, the oldest continuously operating motor speedway in the world, and the Pettit National Ice Center, a US Olympic training rink. Over a century of agricultural exhibitions and motorsport share the same gates.
s: State fairground since 1892, and the world's oldest speedway
_facts: Wisconsin State Fair held here since 1892
Site of the Milwaukee Mile, the oldest continuously operating motor speedway in the world
Also home to the Pettit National Ice Center, a US Olympic training facility
Located in West Allis, a suburb west of Milwaukee
